questions.q: A man using exogenous testosterone has a normal serum testosterone concentration but suppressed LH and low intratesticular testosterone. Which process is most directly compromised?
options: Secretion of inhibin by Sertoli cells only
questions.explain: Exogenous testosterone suppresses hypothalamic GnRH and pituitary LH by negative feedback. Reduced LH stimulation of Leydig cells lowers intratesticular testosterone, which is required at high local concentrations for normal spermatogenesis. A normal serum testosterone concentration does not guarantee adequate intratesticular testosterone.

questions.q: Which pituitary hormone acts directly on Leydig cells to stimulate testosterone synthesis?
questions.explain: Luteinising hormone (LH) stimulates Leydig cells to synthesise testosterone. FSH acts mainly on Sertoli cells, supporting spermatogenesis and stimulating inhibin B production.
